title: Complete higher-prime-power budget for the actual corrected K3 source
summary: Every prime power p^r with r>=2 in the literal corrected gap is priced through its L^2 coefficient, with a bounded remainder. The complete higher-power contribution is eventually positive of order L^5. The ordinary-prime signed covariance remains unbounded by this argument; RH and Step4 remain OPEN.

sections.title: Exact source, compensation and the square bulk
sections.proof:
Keep the actual K3 even/odd vectors, beta=L^2/(16pi^2), Ne=924beta^2+1512beta+1764, No=84beta^2+392beta+724, and a=No/Ne. Let D_L(theta)=E_o(L,theta)-a E_e(L,theta), k_L(t)=D_L(1-t/L) for 0<=t<=L. There is no arbitrary source, test coefficient, or cut-off substitution. The complete canonical gap is
 G(L)=Q_o-aQ_e=A_Gamma(L)+B_1(L)+B_{>=2}(L),
 B_1=-sum_(p<=exp L) log(p)/sqrt(p) k_L(log p),
 B_{>=2}=-sum_(p prime,r>=2,r log p<=L) log(p) p^(-r/2) k_L(r log p).
Prime powers have weight log(p), not r log(p). Unique prime-power factorization makes this a disjoint exact partition of the finite original source, with the same endpoints and floor. The complete corrected rank-one scalar G=80 Re f_source(u_e), both native pole conditions, and the actual Arch channel remain unchanged.

The elementary source matrix integrates on theta in[0,1] to the central-coordinate projector: all off-diagonal sine integrals vanish; for n!=0 integral 2theta cos(2pi n theta)=0; for n=0 the integral is1. Consequently integral E_e=400beta^2 and integral E_o=0, with no central factor2. Hence
 integral_0^L k_L(t)dt=-400a beta^2 L.                    (1)
Also k_L(0)=k_L(L)=k_L'(0)=0. These exact endpoints, rather than an omitted Mertens constant or excluded final prime, pay the square transfer below.

sections.title: A uniform native jet with a fixed error constant
sections.proof:
Set d0=175/(88pi^2). The current source derivatives give E_p'(1)=2|M0(u_p)|^2=0, E_p''(1)=-8pi^2 sum n^2|u_p,n|^2, and E_p'''(1)=-8pi^2[2Re(conj M0 M2)+|M1|^2]=0 for both actual vectors. Let
 Delta=S2o-a S2e, S2o=196beta^2+1448beta+3556, S2e=9No.
Exact polynomial arithmetic gives
 Ne Delta=1555200+2822400beta+3343200beta^2+1041600beta^3+117600beta^4,
 0<=Delta-(1400/11)beta^2<=2048(1+beta).                  (2)

Here is a uniform bound, not a fixed-t asymptotic silently used on a growing interval. For |n|,|m|<=3 and 0<=theta<=1, the fourth theta derivative of each source entry is bounded by2^20. On the diagonal use 2(6pi)^4+8(6pi)^3; off the diagonal use16pi^3(n^4+m^4)/|n-m|, and pi<4. The full 7-by-7 Euclidean norm bound yields |D_L''''|<=14*2^20 No. For L>=1, beta<=L^2 and No<=1200L^4, so |D_L''''|<2^35L^4. Together with (2), pi<4 and Taylor's theorem, the fixed constant C_*=2^34 pays simultaneously, for EVERY L>=1 and 0<=t<=L,
 |k_L(t)+d0 L^2 t^2|<=C_*(t^2+t^4),
 |k_L'(t)+2d0 L^2 t|<=C_*(t+t^3).                       (3)
In particular |k_L(t)|<=(d0+2C_*)L^2t^2 on that same domain. All three estimates use the full moving native coefficients and a(L); no vector is frozen at another aperture.

sections.title: Actual prime Mertens remainder, with every endpoint retained
sections.proof:
Let theta(x)=sum_(p<=x)log p, E_theta(x)=theta(x)-x, and
 W(y)=sum_(p<=exp y) log(p)/p, y>=0.
The classical unconditional quantitative PNT gives |E_theta(x)|<=C x exp(-c sqrt(log x)) after possibly changing constants. To pass from psi to theta, the elementary bound for omitted powers is O(sqrt(x) log(x)^2), which is smaller than that error. The primary PNT input is external analytic authority, not newly formalized here.

Finite Stieltjes summation starting at1, where theta(1)=0, gives
 W(y)=y+c_M+epsilon(y),
 c_M=1+integral_1^infinity E_theta(x)/x^2 dx,
 epsilon(y)=exp(-y)E_theta(exp y)-integral_(exp y)^infinity E_theta(x)/x^2 dx.  (4)
Thus epsilon is locally of bounded variation and has finite absolute polynomial moments; e.g. its late envelope is C(1+sqrt y)exp(-c sqrt y). Define
 M1=integral_0^infinity y epsilon(y)dy,
 J1=integral_0^infinity y|epsilon(y)|dy,
 J3=integral_0^infinity y^3|epsilon(y)|dy.
All are finite and independent of L; M1 is signed. No sign for M1 is assumed. The interval below log2 is retained: W=0 there and epsilon=-y-c_M, in particular epsilon(0)=-c_M. Jumps at actual primes cause no issue because the tested function is C1. This is a fixed arithmetic constant/remainder, not a cutoff-dependent or RH-strength premise.

sections.title: All squares and all exponents at least three, through bounded error
sections.proof:
For the prime-square channel, apply (4) to the exact finite sum:
 B_2(L)=-integral_[0,L/2] k_L(2y)dW(y)
       =200a beta^2 L+2integral_0^(L/2)epsilon(y)k_L'(2y)dy.              (5)
Both endpoint terms vanish by H1, including when exp(L/2) is itself prime. The constant c_M has zero Stieltjes derivative and its integration-by-parts endpoints also vanish. Formula (5) retains the lower prime-free interval, rather than presuming epsilon starts at log2.

By (3), replacing k_L'(2y) by -4d0 L^2 y in (5) costs at most4C_*J1+16C_*J3. Extending the leading moment to infinity costs at most32d0 J3, because y>L/2 implies L^2<=4y^2. Therefore, for all L>=1,
 B_2(L)=200a beta^2 L-8d0 M1 L^2+R_2(L),
 |R_2|<=4C_*J1+(16C_*+32d0)J3.                         (6)

For the entire remaining higher-power channel put
 T_j=sum_(p prime,r>=3) log(p)p^(-r/2)(r log p)^j, j=2,4.
Both sums converge absolutely: summing r first is bounded by a fixed multiple of(log p)^(j+1)p^(-3/2), then compare primes with all integers. T2>0. Formula (3) now gives
 B_{>=3}(L)=d0 T2 L^2+R_3(L),
 |R_3|<=C_*(T2+T4)+d0 T4.                             (7)
The omitted region r log p>L is paid as well: L^2(r log p)^2<=(r log p)^4 there. No missing higher power or unseen cutoff term is hidden in (7). In particular this WHOLE r>=3 contribution is eventually positive, though individual finite terms need not all be positive.

sections.title: An independent signed budget and its exact remaining arithmetic target
sections.proof:
Combining (6)-(7), define the fixed real arithmetic constant H2=T2-8M1. Then
 B_{>=2}(L)=200a(L)beta^2 L+d0 H2 L^2+R_hp(L),           (8)
 |R_hp|<=4C_*J1+(16C_*+32d0)J3+C_*(T2+T4)+d0 T4.
This is a uniform bounded remainder, not O(L^2) left unpaid. The exact rational factor a(L) must stay in the first term: replacing it by1/11 creates an L^3 correction. Since a(L)->1/11,
 B_{>=2}(L) ~ [25/(352pi^4)] L^5 >0.                   (9)
For example B_{>=2}(L)>=[25/(704pi^4)]L^5 eventually for every sufficiently large real L, unconditionally. This signs the COMPLETE higher-prime-power sector using its actual arithmetic, not just one atom. Constants and the final threshold are source/arithmetic-fixed before L varies.

The already reviewed full Arch result is A_Gamma=d0 I2 L^2+O(1), I2=7zeta(3)+pi^3/4. Thus the exact complete target is compressed, with a bounded final error, to
 G(L)=B_1(L)+200a(L)beta^2 L+d0(I2+H2)L^2+O(1).        (10)
No native normal, pole, rank-one or Arch contribution has been discarded. The ordinary-prime sum B_1 is the explicit one in H1, at its original moving aperture and with every prime included. Its compensation of the displayed polynomial is NOT estimated by (10). In particular (9) cannot be applied to the ordinary primes, cannot sign G, and does not imply an eventual polynomial lower bound for G. The prior off-zero excursion and RH cases remain unchanged. This result removes a genuine unpriced subsource; it does not supply the remaining signed closing estimate.

The exact divisor law and Selberg identity were checked against the earlier complete-forcing notes before this calculation. Their generic convolution/positive-storage rewrites are not claimed anew. The new information here is the all-aperture signed polynomial budget (8) for the literal higher-power sector, obtained from exact source moments plus classical PNT. It also falsifies discarding higher powers as merely O(L^2) in this unnormalized K3 target: their actual leading order is positive L^5. No isolated cross-term counterexample, artificial prime sequence, numerical fit, or new RH-equivalent wrapper is used.
